root_cause.text: In `team_queue_override_port_prio_changed()`, the early-return condition incorrectly checked `team_port_enabled(port)` instead of `!team_port_enabled(port)`, so when a disabled port (already removed from the queue override list) had its priority changed, the function attempted to delete it from the list a second time, causing list corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: “3) Port is disabled, queue_id != 0, not in any list 4) Priority changes -> team_queue_override_port_prio_changed() -> checks: port disabled && queue_id != 0 -> calls del - hits the BUG as it is removed already.” The patch changes the condition from `if (!port->queue_id || team_port_enabled(port))` to `if (!port->queue_id || !team_port_enabled(port))`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix inverted condition in team_queue_override_port_prio_changed so queue override updates correctly for enabled ports.
intent_record.what: The condition `team_port_enabled(port)` was changed to `!team_port_enabled(port)` in the if statement.
intent_record.how: Previously, the function returned early (skipping queue override updates) when the port was enabled; now it returns early only when the port is not enabled, allowing updates to proceed for enabled ports with a non-zero queue_id.

grouping_result.intent: Fix inverted condition in team_queue_override_port_prio_changed so queue override updates correctly for enabled ports.

candidates.rationale: The condition incorrectly uses team_port_enabled(port) instead of !team_port_enabled(port), causing early return to be skipped when port is disabled, leading to double deletion from the queue override list and list corruption.
